hints: Think about what marble is made of and what type of chemical attacks it. Focus on acid rain and which gases can form acids in water.
Remember marble is calcium carbonate, $\text{CaCO}_3$, a base that reacts with acids. Only one of these emissions dissolves in rainwater to make nitric acid.
Link high engine temperatures to oxides of nitrogen, then to acid formation, then to carbonate erosion to pick the acidic oxide.
walkthrough:
**Recall what marble is**

Marble is mainly calcium carbonate, $\text{CaCO}_3$. It is a basic carbonate, so it is eroded by acids.

$$\text{CaCO}_3 + 2\text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{Ca}^{2+} + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Recall what engines make at high temperature**

In the very hot engine, nitrogen and oxygen from the air react together to form nitrogen oxides, $\text{NO}$ and $\text{NO}_2$.

$$\text{N}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{NO}$$

**Form acid rain and erode the statue**

Nitrogen dioxide dissolves in rainwater with oxygen to form dilute nitric acid, $\text{HNO}_3$, which is acid rain. This acid then attacks the carbonate statue.

$$4\text{NO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 4\text{HNO}_3$$
$$\text{CaCO}_3 + 2\text{HNO}_3 \rightarrow \text{Ca}(\text{NO}_3)_2 + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

options.A: Carbon monoxide, $\text{CO}$, is toxic because it binds to haemoglobin, but it is neutral and does not form an acid in rainwater. It therefore does not dissolve marble.
options.B: Nitrogen, $\text{N}_2$, makes up about 78% of air and is unreactive under normal conditions. It does not form an acid and does not attack calcium carbonate.
options.C: Nitrogen dioxide, $\text{NO}_2$, is correct. It forms in the engine, dissolves in rain to give nitric acid, and that acid reacts with $\text{CaCO}_3$ in marble to erode it.
options.D: Unburnt hydrocarbons contribute to smog and photochemical pollution, but they do not form strong acids in rainwater. They do not directly erode marble statues.
